channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Moderna’s 160% Surge Burns Shorts in ‘Painful’ $5 Billion Loss
item.description: A record surge in Moderna Inc.’s shares delivered a $5 billion blow to short sellers who had bet that the vaccine maker’s years-long slump would continue.
item.dc:creator: Angel Adegbesan

item.title: Two Sigma Lost ‘Major Investor’ in Founders’ Feud, Overdeck Says
item.description: Two Sigma Investments’ billionaire co-founder John Overdeck said the quantitative hedge fund group lost a “major investor” due to his feud with co-founder David Siegel.
item.dc:creator: Hema Parmar and Chris Dolmetsch

item.title: Carvana Rebounds as Report on Walter’s Pledged Stake Allays Fear
item.description: Shares of online used-car dealer Carvana Co. recovered some losses from a two-day selloff, after a report showed billionaire Mark Walter’s stake in the company was pledged, meaning he wouldn’t be able to immediately sell it as he contends with a federal probe of his investment empire.
item.dc:creator: Georgie McKay

item.title: SpaceX Is Unlocking More Shares. What That Means for Investors.
item.description: SpaceX’s blockbuster $86.2 billion initial public offering on June 11 smashed just about every record there is for new listings. Investors large and small rushed to buy shares in the IPO and get behind Elon Musk’s grand vision for data centers in space, expanded Starlink satellite internet service, artificial intelligence, computer chip manufacturing, space tourism and even asteroid mining.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Hughes

item.title: Alibaba Tops Chinese Tech Stocks This Quarter on AI Resurgence
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. is reclaiming its place as one of investors’ favorite Chinese technology stocks, on bets it can beat rivals in the combative artificial intelligence market.
item.dc:creator: Jeanny Yu and Sunny Bangia

item.title: Harvard Fund Discloses $2.2 Billion Stake in Musk’s SpaceX
item.description: Harvard Management Co. disclosed a $2.2 billion stake in SpaceX, showing how the university’s endowment has profited from an early bet on Elon Musk’s giant rocket company. Janet Lorin, Bloomberg News Higher Education Reporter, discusses the disclosure and what it signals for other university investments. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cantor Becomes To Offer Access To Prediction Market Kalshi
item.description: Cantor Fitzgerald & Co. is giving Wall Street clients access to Kalshi’s prediction markets, in the latest push by the event bets exchange to encourage more institutional involvement in the burgeoning asset class.
item.dc:creator: Bernard Goyder and Felice Maranz

item.title: Bessent Deploys Debt Buybacks in Sign of Concern Over Yield Rise
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent made a fresh attempt to rein-in long-term borrowing costs from multi-year highs, sending Treasury yields and the dollar down. Ira Jersey, Chief US Interest Rates Strategist for Bloomberg Intelligence, discusses the move. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Moderna Surges on Cancer Vaccine; Estee Lauder Rallies on Earnings | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Shares of Moderna (MRNA) surged by a record 101% - the stock’s biggest intraday gain on record - after the biotech said a personalized cancer vaccine combined with partner Merck & Co.’s Keytruda helped cut the recurrence of melanoma in a large, late-stage trial. The study also met a key secondary goal of showing the shot could help prevent tumors from spreading to new areas of the body, the companies said in a statement Wednesday. - Shares of Estee Lauder (EL) rallied after the beauty company’s adjusted earnings per share and sales metrics topped consensus expectations for the fourth quarter. The midpoint of fiscal 2027 organic sales and adjusted EPS guidance ranges are above Street views. - Shares of La-Z-Boy (LZB) tumbled at the open after the furniture maker’s forecast sales for the second quarter missed the average analyst estimate. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Surveillance 8/19/2026
item.description: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ken Fisher’s Firm Seen Behind $4 Billion Contrarian Bond Trade
item.description: Billionaire Ken Fisher’s eponymous firm appears to be betting that the longest-dated US bonds will rally, a contrarian stance that seeks to capitalize on yields close to their highest in two decades.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie and Silla Brush

item.title: Defense-Tech Firm Lyntris Shares Plunge 11% After Downsized IPO
item.description: Lyntris Inc. shares fell 11% in its trading debut, after the company and some of its shareholders raised $297.5 million in a downsized initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Arvelisse Bonilla Ramos

item.title: Target Raises Sales Outlook as Turnaround Gains Strength
item.description: Joe Feldman, senior research analyst and assistant director of research at Telsey, says there is a “strong signal that the turnaround is working” at Target. The retailer lifted its full-year guidance after results outpaced estimates in the second-quarter. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jefferies Targets €1 Billion for Private Credit Secondaries Fund
item.description: Jefferies Credit Partners is seeking to raise around €1 billion ($1.16 billion) from investors who trade private credit in the secondary market.
item.dc:creator: Kat Hidalgo

item.title: Hedge Fund Capula Hires From Freepoint, Element in Energy Push
item.description: Capula Investment Management hired two energy traders as it expands into energy and commodities, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Eamon Akil Farhat and Liza Tetley

item.title: Target’s Turnaround Is Finally Working: Telsey Analyst
item.description: Target’s turnaround may finally be working. Telsey Advisory Group Senior Managing Director and Assistant Director of Research Joseph Feldman joined Bloomberg Open Interest to break down why stronger traffic, sharper merchandising and a revamped food strategy are bringing shoppers back, even without tariff refunds. He also explains why Target shouldn’t copy Walmart and which struggling retailers could lose the most market share. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dollar Tumbles to Weakest in Three Months on Treasury Buyback
item.description: The dollar tumbled by the most in three weeks after the Trump administration’s unexpected bond buyback announcement reversed a Treasury market rout that had pushed long-dated yields to the highest since 2007.
item.dc:creator: Anya Andrianova

item.title: Bessent Deploys Debt Buybacks in Sign of Concern Over Yield Rise
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent made a fresh attempt to rein-in long-term borrowing costs from multi-year highs, sending Treasury yields and the dollar down.
item.dc:creator: Michael MacKenzie and Greg Ritchie

item.title: Stocks Climb as Treasury Steps In to Support Bonds: Markets Wrap
item.description: Wall Street staged a rebound after the Treasury said it plans to boost buybacks of longer-dated bonds, a signal the US wants to lower borrowing costs after yields hit multi-decade highs.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 19
item.description: Oil rose to the highest in almost three weeks, as US refiners ramped up crude consumption and a spat between the United Arab Emirates and Iran heightened regional tensions.
item.dc:creator: Charles Gorrivan and Grant Smith
